hook_text: A rectangle, a diagonal, two equal triangles. Looks symmetric. Fold it and watch it fail.
clip_script: Cut out a rectangle. Draw the diagonal. Two equal triangles, so it must be a line of symmetry, right? Fold it. The corners stick out, the long side lands on the short side, nothing matches. Equal halves are not symmetry. Now fold the rectangle down the middle: left half onto right half, edge on edge, corner on corner. That is a line of symmetry. The rectangle has two, up and across. A square has four, because its diagonals work too. Now letters. A folds down the middle. B folds across. H folds both ways. S looks balanced but fails every fold; it has a different kind of balance, turning balance. The test is always the same: fold it, and the halves must sit exactly on top of each other. If anything sticks out, it is not a line of symmetry.
visual_style: Whiteboard rectangle folding along its diagonal with corners overhanging in red, then folding down the middle and matching in green; letters folding one by one.
mood: Myth busted, then the clean rule.
pacing: The diagonal fails, the middle fold works, the square's four lines, letters in a quick run, then the rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write your name in capitals, then find which letters have a line of symmetry.
